tasks.behavior: Tokens sent to the invoice receiver factory can be returned by the refund authority

notes: 2026-11-06 review fail by reviewer: Fail on one money-safety gap. After the hold, useSendApproval sets working but calls onSigning(true) only after approve answers (use-send-approval.ts:43-60). While approve is in flight (a Privy call on a fresh session, or the repeat after a confirmed code) the sheet is not locked and Back shows (send-sheet.tsx:169,508,510). Closing sends cancel, but if approve read the send first, Privy still signs it with the sheet closed, and the server may never hold the hash; Back to change the amount can likewise sign the old send. The old Review locked from the click. Fix: lock close and hide Back while approval.working and no confirm step shows (or drop the sign when the attempt was abandoned), with a unit test. Also fix: base.css:183 comment still describes --fw-step-x and slides; R-213 still says the button reads Send 5 USDC and R-214 says pressed, now Hold to send. Should-fix: HoldButton has no path for screen readers in browse mode, which click instead of key or pointer down. Rest looks right: approve gates signing on status prepared, base units via BigInt, one send per hold, FreshSignIn on approve only, openapi and api.md match, EIP-55 check, StepTransition fade with motion-safe, hold fill marked essential. 2026-11-06 review pass by reviewer: Pass. 9d06b55c is correct. wallet-screen.tsx:52-53 closes the warning and clears opening before awaiting exportWallet, so a pending Privy promise can't leave Show the key busy. Privy 3.51.0 confirms the premise: Escape calls onUserCloseViaDialogOrKeybindRef, which resolves the export, but modal-context nulls that ref on each screen change, so the promise can stay pending. Each Show runs fresh.run (Confirm it's you) again. A rejected exportWallet still shows the danger toast (unit test 3). A second open just replaces Privy's modal data; the old promise is dropped, no double window. The new unit test fails before the fix: Button sets aria-busy while loading and ignores clicks, and the old finally never ran. wallet.spec.ts closes Privy with Escape, checks the button is not busy, and reopens Privy's window. No doc describes the loading state, so no doc change is needed. The comment gives a non-obvious reason. No AI attribution in branch commits. Note, not blocking: wallet-screen.test.tsx:83 could also assert calls.check ran twice. Ran: vitest src/screens/wallet -> 5 passed; pnpm lint, pnpm typecheck, check-docs -> passed.

2026-11-06 review fail by reviewer: Fail, 1 fix (plus 1 minor). Permission, flow and docs are sound: /app/wallet needs money.move in MENU_PAGES, so settings hides it and app-shell redirects a member; the check runs before exportWallet; docs match the code; unit tests (26), lint and typecheck pass. (1) apps/web/src/screens/wallet/wallet-screen.tsx:420-424: closing Privy's window while it still shows Connecting to your wallet shows a red toast 'The export page didn't open. Try again.' Privy 3.51.0 EmbeddedWalletConnectingScreen wires its close button and Escape to onFailure('User exited before wallet could be connected'), which rejects exportWallet. The connecting step lasts at least 1 s. A user cancel must not read as a failure. Treat that rejection as a cancel (no toast) and add a unit test where exportWallet rejects with it. Closing on the key screen calls onSuccess, so it is fine. (2, minor) apps/web/e2e/privy/wallet.spec.ts:43 (and the copied pattern in passkeys.spec.ts:10): locator.isVisible ignores its timeout in Playwright 1.64 and returns at once. The Confirm it's you step appears only after the check's 401 round trip, so with a stale shared session (over 15 min, D-49) the branch is skipped and the test fails at the dialog-hidden expect. Use confirm.waitFor({ timeout }) with a catch instead. Commits carry no AI attribution.
